newsitem.title: USA: Last U.S. food aid arriving in North Korea.
newsitem.headline: Last U.S. food aid arriving in North Korea.

text.p: The last of the U.S. food aid so far allocated to famine-threatened North Korea is about to arrive in the hard-hit northeastern part of the country, the State Department said on Thursday.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said a U.S. ship unloaded 17,000 tons of grain June 29 in Nampo on North Korea's west coast and was now proceeding to Chongjin in northeastern North Korea where it would deliver a further 8,000 tons.
The two deliveries are the last in a U.S. aid programme that has so far amounted to $25 million this year in response to appeals from the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP).

Burns said this was the first international aid shipment to be delivered directly to northeastern North Korea, and Pyongyang had agreed that the WFP could send monitors to that region for the first time.
"So we're satisfied that both sides are carrying out their commitments in the provision of food assistance," he told a news briefing.

The Rome-based WFP said on Tuesday it had received almost all the $95.5 million it had requested in its latest appeal to prevent famine in North Korea, hit by flooding which destroyed rice crops in 1995-96.
Pyongyang has said it requires still more food aid. The United States has repeatedly said that it will consider any further appeals by the WFP but none have so far been made.
